newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Arafat-Netanyahu summit doubtful on Tuesday.
newsitem.headline: Arafat-Netanyahu summit doubtful on Tuesday.

text.p: PLO officials said Palestinian President Yasser Arafat and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu were "most unlikely" to hold their first summit on Tuesday despite marathon efforts to arrange a meeting.

"It is most unlikely Arafat will meet Netanyahu today," one official said. He and other PLO officials accused the Israelis of refusing to commit to agreements signed by the government which Netanyahu ousted in May.
"The Israelis are still insisting on modifying agreements and are not willing to commit themselves to implementation of the Oslo accords," a PLO official said.
Israeli Cabinet Secretary Danny Naveh said he could not say when a meeting might take place but told Israeli army radio: "We're making progress towards this agreement."
Contacts continued into the night after Arafat threatened to seek international arbitration if Israeli-PLO attempts to resume full-fledged peace negotiations faltered.

The Palestinians are seeking a clear commitment from Netanyahu to implement all outstanding issues in Israel-PLO peace deals, such as Israeli troop redeployment from Hebron and other parts of the West Bank, a PLO official said.
